title: Learning to Solve Hard Problems in RL for LLMs by Never Giving Up
abstract: arXiv:2609.13443v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: We demonstrate that training LLMs with RL does not improve performance equally across a dataset. RL shows large improvements on easy problems that an LLM is already good at solving, but small improvements on hard problems. We call this the Matthew Effect in RL for LLMs, after the phenomenon of cumulative advantage from economics and network science summarized as "the rich get richer". The naive explanation is that hard problems require more compute to find a solution. We argue that modern RL methods are exacerbating the issue by wasting too much compute on easy problems and instead should dynamically reallocate how they use compute. We introduce Never Give Up (NGU), a simple adaptive sampling method that keeps generating samples for a problem until one is correct. By leveraging asynchronous RL, this naturally uses fewer samples to filter out easy problems and allocates more compute to solving harder problems. We investigate the design

translated_title: 通过永不放弃学习解决LLM强化学习中的困难问题
translated_abstract: 我们证明使用强化学习训练大型语言模型并不会在数据集上均匀地提升性能。RL在LLM已经擅长解决的简单问题上显示出巨大的改进，但在困难问题上的改进很小。我们将这种现象称为LLM强化学习中的马太效应，这一名称源于经济学和网络科学中被总结为“富者愈富”的累积优势现象。一种天真的解释是困难问题需要更多计算才能找到解决方案。我们认为现代RL方法通过在简单问题上浪费过多计算而加剧了这一问题，相反应该动态重新分配计算的使用方式。我们提出了永不放弃（NGU），这是一种简单的自适应采样方法，它会持续为一个问题生成样本直到得到正确答案。通过利用异步RL，该方法自然地使用更少的样本来过滤掉简单问题，并将更多计算分配给解决更困难的问题。我们研究了该设计
tldr: 本文发现LLM强化学习训练存在“马太效应”——简单问题提升大而困难问题提升小，并提出自适应采样方法NGU，通过持续为一个问题采样直到得到正确答案，将更多计算资源动态分配给困难问题。
